findings.quote: either with two parents (sexual) or with one parent (asexual)
findings.problem: This defines sexual reproduction by the number of parents, and the definition fails at a standard exception: self-pollination and self-fertilization (Mendel's pea plants, hermaphrodite animals) are sexual reproduction with one parent, because gametes fuse. A student who learns this rule will call self-pollination asexual. The base lesson said only 'sexually or asexually' and had no such rule.
findings.source: OpenStax Biology 2e, 32.2 Pollination and Fertilization (self-pollination) and 43.1 Reproduction Methods (sexual reproduction is the fusion of gametes, usually from two individuals; self-fertilization in hermaphrodites); reader-rules.md, Added after the Sol audit

findings.quote: Fire and crystals match one property each.
findings.problem: False for fire, and it contradicts the lesson's own Core Concept, which says 'Fire consumes fuel, grows, and spreads': energy use and growth at least. Fire is the standard case of a nonliving thing that copies several properties of life. Telling students it copies only one invites them to judge life by counting properties instead of by the missing cells.
findings.source: Lesson Core Concept line 'Fire consumes fuel, grows, and spreads.'; reader-rules.md, Added after the Sol audit (test each 'each' statement); content-checklist B01

findings.quote: A dry seed does not grow, move, or react for a long time. It is still alive.
findings.problem: This paragraph has six sentences. Paragraphs must be one to three short sentences. Other paragraphs also run over: the Core Concept opening, Cellular organization, Reproduction, Evolutionary adaptation, the first virus paragraph, and the paragraph after the levels list each have four or five sentences.
